title: A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums
summary: Let $m(p)$ be the least size of a subset of $\F_p$ with at least two elements for which every sum has two distinct representations as unordered pairs, allowing repetition. We prove that, for every prime $p\ge64$, \[ m(p)\ge2^{-80}\left(\frac{\log p}{\log\log p}\right)^2. \] The argument compresses the full integer collision lattice by unit-pivot elimination. A shared random sample and forests of bounded diameter give $O(\sqrt n+n/\log p)$ surviving coordinates of polynomial height for a minimal set of size $n$.
